clue.text: Doctors swear by this new Ai orthoptic chap

indicators.note: new tells us these three words are to be made afresh in another order

explanation.surface: An oath taken by a man treating eye muscles, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges AI ORTHOPTIC CHAP; an ai is a three-toed sloth, a crossword regular. The page reads 'Al', a scanning slip for 'Ai'.
explanation.definitionFit: Newly qualified physicians traditionally pledge the ancient Greek ethical promise named after the father of medicine.

clue.text: Tense, being very old on stage

parts.note: something very old belongs to history, so historic
an actor on stage is present before the audience

explanation.surface: An elderly actor still treading the boards, and nervous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the nervous old actor, but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: This grammatical form narrates past events using present-time verbs for vividness.

clue.text: Uncomplaining invalid

definitions.meaning: uncomplaining means enduring calmly without fuss
an invalid is a sick person under a doctor's care

explanation.definitionFit: One word is the adjective for calm forbearance and also the noun for someone receiving medical treatment.

clue.text: Work to give oxygen to Manx cat?

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: Giving a tailless cat some oxygen as a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' cuts the tail off PUSS, leaving PUS; the Manx breed from the Isle of Man is tailless.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer's numbered compositions are each labelled with this Latin term for a piece.

clue.text: Announce data from computer

definitions.meaning: to announce is to say something publicly from a script
a printed or displayed record of a machine's output

explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means to speak aloud a list; as a noun it is a display of information from a machine.

clue.text: Crossbar on trams, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters of on trams turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A bar fitted across the tops of tramcars, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges ON TRAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: In building, this is the horizontal beam above a door or window.

clue.text: Struggle through work in church

indicators.note: in places the word for work inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Labouring hard at a job in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OP inside CE. The answer is also a priest's cloak, which helps the church picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or get by under difficulty is to deal with it successfully.

clue.text: High post?

parts.note: post here means letters carried, and high means sent through the sky by plane

explanation.definitionFit: Mail flown by aeroplane travels at altitude, so it is lofty correspondence.

clue.text: Touching the shot-an offence at Stamford Bridge?

definitions.text: Touching the shot-an offence at Stamford Bridge?

parts.words: Touching the shot-an offence at Stamford Bridge?
parts.note: Stamford Bridge is Chelsea's football ground, where touching the ball with the hands is a foul; it is also a way a cricket batsman can be out

explanation.walkthrough: Stamford Bridge is the London stadium of Chelsea Football Club, not the 1066 battle site.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately using a hand on the ball breaks the laws of football and was once a mode of dismissal in cricket.

clue.text: Mandarin in a loose jacket-a necessity, as in retirement

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing backwards, so the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: a must is something you cannot do without

explanation.surface: A Chinese official in a baggy coat insists on retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns A MUST AS backwards. 'Mandarin' looks like an official but is the fruit, whose skin is easily peeled.
explanation.definitionFit: This loose-skinned citrus is a variety of the small orange family.

clue.text: Endlessly craving drug in common use

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for craving loses its final letter

parts.note: aspiring means longing or striving for

explanation.surface: An addict's constant longing for an everyday medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the last G from ASPIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: This painkiller, acetylsalicylic acid, is among the most widely taken medicines.

clue.text: Frank to set up shop?

definitions.meaning: to start trading for the day, unlocking the doors

explanation.definitionFit: One word means candid and also to begin business.

clue.text: Lift from Crouch End roundabout? It's arranged!

indicators.note: end picks out the final letter of the word Crouch

parts.note: a roundabout is circular, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of It's are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A lift home from Crouch End, a north London district, via the roundabout is all set up.
explanation.walkthrough: Crouch End is a district of north London; 'End' takes its last letter, H. 'arranged' reorders ITS into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something, usually with ropes or tackle, is a synonym of elevate.

clue.text: Round dance

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a sphere and also a grand formal dancing party.

clue.text: Moribund old wife leaves the heap

indicators.note: leaves means goes out of, so those letters depart from Moribund

parts.note: Eve was made from Adam's rib, so rib is a jocular old word for a wife

explanation.surface: A dying old woman walks out on the pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes RIB from MORIBUND; RIB for wife comes from Eve being made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile or raised bank of earth is a synonym for a heap.

clue.text: Strange card-game

definitions.meaning: old British slang for odd or peculiar
a game of collecting sets and runs of cards

explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for peculiar is also a popular game of melding sets.

clue.text: Part of the Mass, or short prelude to it

parts.note: intro is a shortened form of introduction, a prelude

explanation.surface: A section of the church service, or a brief opening for it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the opening chant or psalm sung as the priest enters at the start of the Eucharist.

clue.text: Foolishly sentimental in Oxford College, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the college's name is said out loud

parts.note: Magdalen is an Oxford college, pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: Weepy and soft-headed in an Oxford college, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear': Magdalen College, Oxford, is pronounced 'maudlin', a famous quirk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearfully or drunkenly over-emotional describes mawkish behaviour.

clue.text: Workers in coal-mine ring for allspice

indicators.note: in places the workers inside the coal-mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal-mine
men are workers, as in management and men
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Miners in the pit form a ring around the spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MEN inside PIT, giving PIMENT, then O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is another name for the Jamaican pepper berry also sold as allspice.

clue.text: Minorca-resort of an early signaller

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort the letters of Minorca again

explanation.surface: A Balearic holiday resort associated with a pioneer of signalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but means re-sort, rearranging MINORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi pioneered long-distance radio telegraphy around 1900.

clue.text: Lear's daughter in spectacles, displays marjoram

indicators.note: in puts the daughter inside the spectacles

parts.note: a pair of spectacles looks like two letter Os
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: King Lear's daughter, wearing glasses, shows off a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts REGAN inside OO, the two lenses of a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild marjoram is the common name for the herb used in Mediterranean cooking.

clue.text: Firm agreement?

definitions.meaning: firm means solid and closely packed
a formal pact or treaty between parties

explanation.definitionFit: One word means dense and solid and also a pact between parties.

clue.text: Endless ecology, perhaps, about northern European city

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the northern letter
perhaps suggests the remaining letters could be in another order
endless means the word ecology loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Unending environmental concern around a city in northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops Y from ECOLOGY; 'perhaps' rearranges ECOLOG; 'about' sets those letters round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne, or Koln, is a major German city on the Rhine.

clue.text: Abstainer-difficult case with nervous twitch

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters of case are twisted

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary nervous spasm

explanation.surface: A teetotaller, a hard case with a twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' reorders CASE into ASCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who renounces worldly pleasures practises severe self-denial.

clue.text: Leicester, for example, ahead of time almost

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of complete

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Leicester, a city, nearly arrives before schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of EARLY. Leicester is not the city here: Robert Dudley was Earl of Leicester.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester names a noble title, as in Robert Dudley, Elizabeth I's favourite.

clue.text: Writer's sources?

definitions.meaning: the writer is H. G. ..., author of The Time Machine; the 's stands for is
sources of water dug in the ground

explanation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells was a novelist, and springs or bores where water rises are water sources.

clue.text: Area of field used for medley race

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters of race are mixed

explanation.surface: A patch of field set aside for a mixed relay race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley' looks like a swimming race but rearranges RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a unit of land measure, 4,840 square yards.

clue.text: If retired, look after dog

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the word If is read backwards

parts.note: to do someone is to care for them, as in do for

explanation.surface: If the owner retires, someone must mind the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns IF into FI. DO for 'look after' is like 'do for', to keep house for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fido is the stock name for a pet dog.

clue.text: To drink noisily (not quietly) S is a stain on one's reputation

indicators.note: not tells us the quiet letter is left out

parts.note: to slurp is to drink with a loud sucking noise
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Gulping soup loudly is a black mark on one's character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes P (piano) from SLURP. The stray 'S' in the clue as held looks like a scanning mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An insult or slight that damages good name is an aspersion.

clue.text: Tempo in Beethoven symphony may excite people

indicators.note: in puts the tempo letter inside the symphony

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony
T is an abbreviation for tempo

explanation.surface: The beat of a Beethoven symphony may stir listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T inside EROICA. The definition is loose: material that may arouse people.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexually explicit art or literature is meant to arouse its audience.

clue.text: Celebration drink for this production of Pygmalion?

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A party drink for the first night of Shaw's Pygmalion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of Pygmalion' suggests Shaw's play, but in Greek myth Pygmalion sculpted a statue that came to life.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the sculptor's ivory statue, brought to life, came to be called by this name.

clue.text: New motoring article dealing with functions of angles

indicators.note: new means the letters of motoring and article are formed into something fresh

explanation.surface: A fresh feature about driving on the mathematics of angles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges MOTORING ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine, cosine and tangent are the subject of this branch of mathematics.
